metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after spikes or volatility; reduce initial forecast peaks by 5–15%.
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward; apply a “cool-down” adjustment: subtract 2–5% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.
- When sentiment is neutral or flat (all 0.00), model exhibits high volatility and overconfidence; cap forecast range within ±3% of recent 7-day moving average.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast exceeds 20% above recent 14-day high, reduce by 10–20% unless driven by confirmed event.
- If true outcome shows downward trend after a peak, model often fails to recognize it; apply lag correction: shift forecast 1–2 days backward if price drops >3% from peak.
- In absence of sentiment signals, model overweights historical momentum; reduce weight of recent 3–5 day highs in forecasting if no event context is present.
